title: ticket-lease-queueing-scheme to reduce KV-heavy starvation in continuous batcher
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: we observe persistent tail latency regressions in mixed workloads where KV-heavy requests hold pins and block continuously batched windows. Previous fixes (cohorting, timeout guards) reduced some cases but left intermittent starvation when request sizes and arrival patterns create long-lived head-of-queue holds. This PR implements a lightweight ticket+lease scheme for the continuous batcher that enforces bounded queue-hold time, improves dequeue fairness across request classes, and enables controlled lease extension for low-latency short workloads.

Design summary: single-threaded ticket assignment per incoming request, short lease token assigned at enqueue, scheduler uses ticket age and lease state to decide coalescing vs. early-dequeue; a skew-aware penalty function gradually deprioritizes requests that repeatedly requeue due to KV pin conflicts; support for an optional per-model lease-duration override; metrics and traces for ticket lifecycle. No API surface changes.

Checklist: 
- [x] design doc linked (ENG-5173)
- [x] unit tests covering ticket lifecycle and penalty decay
- [x] integration test with simulated KV-pin contention
- [x] bench suite run against internal mixed workload harness
- [x] docs: brief explainer in serving/README.md

Rollout plan: feature gated behind runtime flag `continuous_batcher.ticket_lease_enabled` (off by default for dedicated early customers). Start with 10% canary on redwood-hosted inference for internal testing, observe tail p99/P95 and KV lock-duration metrics for two weeks, then progressive ramp if stable.

Behavioral notes: 
- Normal short text-only requests get short default leases (8ms) and are favored for coalescing.
- KV-heavy requests receive initial short lease but may request a single lease-extension via a lightweight handshake; extensions are rate-limited per-client to avoid head-of-line monopolization.
- Requests that hit their max-retry penalty window are evicted into a separate slow-path queue that gets scheduled at fixed small intervals to guarantee forward progress (prevents starvation).

Benchmarks (mixed workload synthesizer): 
- 95th latency on mixed KV-heavy test: improved from 142ms -> 116ms (18% reduction)
- 99th latency: improved from 312ms -> 256ms (18% reduction)
- Overall throughput under nominal load: +6% due to reduced queuing hold time
- Microbench: ticket allocation overhead ~0.6us per request in hot paths (measured on c6g-gpu infra).

Compatibility and safety: the scheme is conservative by default (short leases, single extension). Configurable knobs documented in serving/configuration.md. No model-format changes. Fallback: when disabled, scheduler reverts to previous coalescer behavior.

Related work: references prior PRs on fairness and timeout guards (see ENG-4211, PRs in 60000-65000 range).

Notes: this PR focuses on scheduler heuristics and bookkeeping; a follow-up will expose telemetry-driven auto-tuning of lease durations and penalty backoff constants.
